tests.name: TestStatusRecoveringRoundTrip
tests.title: Saved RECOVERING execution is read back with status RECOVERING and error preserved
tests.scenario: Given a new store in a temp dir, when an execution with Status RECOVERING and Error "boom" is saved and fetched by ID, then Status equals "RECOVERING" and Error equals "boom"
tests.detail: PASS in 0.00s; the constant already existed, so this is a coverage-only test that passes on first run.

units.title: Verify: Recover scan and resume unit tests with fake store

tests.name: TestRecoverResumesOnlyUnfinished
tests.title: Recover resumes only PENDING, RUNNING and RECOVERING executions and saves nothing
tests.scenario: Given executions a-pending, b-running, c-recovering, d-done, e-failed and f-await; When Recover runs; Then resumer IDs and Result.Resumed equal [a-pending b-running c-recovering] and fs.saved is empty

tests.name: TestRecoverListError
tests.title: Recover returns the wrapped store list error and resumes nothing
tests.scenario: Given the store List call fails with errors.New("disk"); When Recover runs; Then errors.Is(err, listErr) holds and the resumer records no IDs

units.title: Verify: Failed resume marks RECOVERING unit tests with fake clock

tests.name: TestRecoverMarksFailedResume
tests.title: Recover marks a failed resume as RECOVERING with the error and clock time, and only resumes the other execution
tests.scenario: Given a RUNNING execution whose resume fails and a second RUNNING execution whose resume succeeds, When Recover runs with a fixed clock, Then the failed one is saved as RECOVERING with error text and the fixed UpdatedAt, the resumer was called with [a-run b-run], Result.Marked is [a-run] and Result.Resumed is [b-run].

tests.name: TestRecoverSaveFailure
tests.title: Recover returns an error wrapping the save error when persisting a failed resume fails
tests.scenario: Given a RUNNING execution whose resume fails and a store whose Save fails, When Recover runs, Then the returned error satisfies errors.Is with the save error.

units.title: Verify: Stale lock release and Startup unit tests with fake clock

tests.name: TestStartupReleasesStaleLock
tests.title: Startup removes a stale lock, reports LockReleased, and resumes the RUNNING execution
tests.scenario: Given a lock modified 2h before a fixed clock with StaleAfter 1h and one RUNNING execution, When Startup runs, Then removed is [w/lock], LockReleased is true and run-1 is resumed

tests.name: TestStartupKeepsFreshOrMissingLock
tests.title: Startup keeps a fresh or missing lock, with no removal, LockReleased false and no error
tests.scenario: Given a lock modified 10m ago, or ModTime returning fs.ErrNotExist, When Startup runs, Then nothing is removed, LockReleased is false and err is nil

tests.name: TestStartupRemoveFailureStopsRecovery
tests.title: Startup returns the stale-lock remove error and resumes no execution
tests.scenario: Given a stale lock whose Remove fails with 'perm' and one RUNNING execution, When Startup runs, Then errors.Is(err, removeErr) holds and the resumer recorded no IDs
